handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own credential layer. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal: SecretEnv ACTION1_OAUTH2, ACTION1_CLIENT_SECRET and ACTION1_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN; the client ID an identifier with its unique part held (holdClientID); config.toml and the 0600 credentials.toml named in Files and written outside the kit as a declared exemption; /oauth2/token and 2FA setup response fields declared; base_url the one allowed origin. credkit.Start is the first statement and credkit.Exit the last of both mains. Outbound requests go through credkit.Transport under the origin pin, files through credkit.WriteFile/AppendFile/OpenFile, SQLite through credkit.SQLDriver (internal/credsql), the MCP server through MCPTools/MCPIn/MCPOut/MCPHTTP, child processes through credkit.RunCommand.

The connector's own holder, output chokepoint, secret funnel, encodings and scattered matchers, store withholding driver and MCP output wrappers grew per review round because each sink and encoding was closed one at a time; the kit is one reviewed implementation, and it closes the print's three open credential classes: the journal record is checked whole with its timestamp, a short value is matched in every decoded view, and a value split across MCP messages is withheld piece by piece. The client ID is an identifier because Action1 issues it as api-key-<uuid>@action1.com: held whole, its 8-character pieces would withhold every line naming action1.com, the API host included.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For action1 the manifest gained: ACTION1_BASE_URL, ACTION1_OAUTH2, ACTION1_ORG_ID. Phantom prompt(s) the binary never reads were removed: ACTION1_REGION. server.json gained: ACTION1_BASE_URL, ACTION1_OAUTH2, ACTION1_ORG_ID. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: ACTION1_BASE_URL, ACTION1_OAUTH2, ACTION1_ORG_ID. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: ACTION1_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth set-token`, the only command on this connector that writes a credential on purpose (its `auth --help` lists logout, set-token, setup, status), REFUSES and names the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) newMCPClient now resolves through config.Load(""), the resolver the CLI uses, so the MCP server honours both ACTION1_CONFIG and this switch; that is the half the issue says is uncovered today. The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and the MCP server resolving its config through config.Load("") instead of a hardcoded home-relative path. The hardcoded path in internal/mcp/tools.go is a generator defect in its own right - it makes --config and <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

asserts.contains: | `auth set-token` | Refuses, naming the variable, instead of reporting a save that did not happen. |

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 3 commands listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs them
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: automations policies-instances-org-id-instance-id-stop-post (POST /automations/instances/{orgId}/{instanceId}/stop); enterprise request-closure (POST /enterprise/request-closure); updates approvals updates-org-id (POST /updates/{orgId}/approvals).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: export --output closes its (withholding) output file on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows RunE's named err
handfixes.why: The generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` inside the --output block declared a new err, so the deferred close tested that inner (nil) err and never ran when the export returned an API error. With the output chokepoint the file is a filter pipe, and the unclosed pipe kept the process from exiting: `export clients --output f.jsonl` after a 401 hung (TestExportOutputReturnsAfterAnAPIError, seen failing 3 of 4 runs). Fleet note: every connector that took the ported chokepoint edit on export.go carries the same shadowing. Ported to action1 from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet).

handfixes.summary: ACTION1_CLIENT_ID + ACTION1_CLIENT_SECRET mint the bearer token automatically: POST <base URL>/oauth2/token with a JSON body (refresh_token grant when a refresh token exists), on the API origin through the guarded client, one mint at a time; the env pair is an environment override never written to disk (configForSave restores the file values), counts for the untrusted-config refusal, and is held with the minted tokens; a rejected mint returns with only a validated RFC 6749 error code
handfixes.why: Action1's spec declares an OAuth2 password flow, but the real grant is client credentials with a JSON body (shipped since the first print as internal/client/oauth_cc.go). Press 4.34.2 renders only ACTION1_OAUTH2 for this scheme, so without the Load lines no client pair is read and every command is unauthenticated; the authHeader hook mints. Rewritten for 4.34.2: the 0600 credential store holds the minted token, EnvOverride drops an unresolved .mcpb placeholder, mintMu stops concurrent org fan-out requests minting in parallel (and racing on the config fields), and the token request goes to the base URL's own region host.

handfixes.summary: A stored access token is owned by the client named in the record that supplied it (config file, a --config file's own credentials, or the global credential store), not by the merged configuration; a token is cached only into a global record that is this client's (or none, without --config), so a --config pair never sends or overwrites another client's token

Ownership now comes from the record. Generated config.go carries four one-line calls into hand code in action1_tokens.go.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name. The ACTION1_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>:" plus the typed name's hash when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. Operator-named text that repeats a credential the program holds (a profile, the journal, teach.log, learnings.jsonl, feedback.jsonl, the learn tables) is withheld by the shared credential kit at the sink (credkit-wiring). journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path, holds through the kit in its held pass, and fails if a credential reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) returns the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, and records every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query. These are names the kit never holds, so they stay hand-fixes. Seen failing on the pre-kit tree (115873121, .review/seen/prewire-journal.log: the raw session key, argv after --, the typed flag kept and failed flags not opaque) and passing after; the shape and tests follow rocketcyber's entry of the same id. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments.

handfixes.summary: credkit.Start is the first statement of both mains (credkit-wiring), so every credential in config.toml is held before the program can print a byte, a config that does not parse included: the kit reads the whole file, and where a declared credential key, headers, auth_header or base_url is followed by a separator it holds the value after it. A credential in a malformed config.toml (an unquoted bare value, a valid line then a broken table, a credential after 64 KiB of padding, inside auth_header, inside [headers]) or in a base_url that does not parse never appears in action1-cli startup output (stdout and stderr, plain and --json; doctor and vendor get) or in action1-mcp's stderr and JSON-RPC responses, for the discovered default config and an explicit one (--config, ACTION1_CONFIG for the MCP server). A run the kit refuses to start (exit 78) prints no credential either.
handfixes.why: Fleet rule (Startup ordering): the holder must be installed before config is loaded or any startup diagnostic can print, in both the CLI and the MCP server, and a config that fails to parse still has every value in it held. internal/credwire/startup_test.go TestStartupConfigHeldFirst builds and runs both binaries (.exe on Windows) under ACTION1_HOME in a sandbox. Proved both ways: with credkit.Start removed from both mains the base_url case fails (the URL parse error prints its password; .review/seen/mutant-startup-no-kit.log), and it passes with the kit. The TOML parser's own errors name no value, so the five malformed-file cases pass with or without a holder; they stay as the contract's named inputs.

handfixes.summary: The press test TestMirroredDestructiveCommandRefusesWithoutYes judges a hung destructive MCP call by whether its context deadline fired (callHung, 30 s), not by elapsed wall time over 2 s.
handfixes.why: On PR #598 the Windows CI row failed it with 'destructive call hung for 2.569s': the first exec of the probe binary the test had just compiled was slow on a loaded runner while the probe answered at once (0.3 s locally). A child blocked on a confirmation prompt still runs into the deadline and fails the test. TestCallHungJudgesTheDeadlineNotTheClock (hand file action1_hang_test.go) proves both ways: a probe that sleeps 2.5 s then refuses fails the old wall-clock check (.review/seen/hang-before.log) and passes callHung; a probe that never answers is judged hung. 64 connectors carry the same press test; a fleet fix belongs upstream in the press template.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored, sync keeps walking, and the run still succeeds, naming the row ids on stderr and in its summary
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows). synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row no longer fails the resource. mcp2 measured hubspot-calls-crm row 80663490159 turning the whole sync into exit 1, so the server never marked the connector synced. Now the resource ends stored with the ids named (stderr warning, a sync_warning rows_withheld event per page, and "withheld" in the summary), the run exits 0 when every other row stored, and the resource's checkpoint stays where the attempt began so the next run fetches the row again.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).
